letters.title: Robert D. Roberts to Evan W. Roberts - 22 February 1915
letters.language: English supplied translation/transcription; underlying letter language not established
letters.suppliedText:
891-897
Logan City
22 February, 1915
Evan W. Roberts
Dear Cousin
I got your letter dated 11th February. Thank you for thinking about me and, as I am not currently busy with work, I will
try to reply. I will collect my thoughts and find acceptable and understandable language and ask for a wise spirit to
help me. I do not feel very confident in writing - I tend to make spelling mistakes and my mind is not as strong and as
stable as it was in days gone by.
Myself and the children are quite healthy. My sister Jane has not been too well but is now improving. Ann likewise has
not been too strong. David and family are in good spirits. As I understand it, Thomas has not been too well as a result
of getting a chill but he is improving at the moment; he has a wife and two children.
This area has been very successful this past year. But at this time of year there is not much work around – hundreds in
Salt Lake City and Utah are unemployed. The weather has been mild this past winter. I cannot remember any time
when people felt more optimistic though.
I got a letter from William Daniel Roberts, the son of our uncle from Troy County (the other two children are Robert
and Elizabeth) and they are all in good health and doing quite well. I also received a letter from Ellis Roberts from
Penrhyn – the son of Uncle Robert. It is possible that he will come to the fair in San Francisco, California quite soon.
That's about all our news for you.
It is likely that, very soon, the children and great grandchildren of our grandfather, will have spread out so much that it
will be difficult to trace and they will be strangers to one another.
Permit me at this time to draw to your attention to the Bible and Joseph Smith.
In your letter, you said things against President Wilson. Now let me draw your attention to some verses from the Bible.
I will be as succinct as possible because I do not want to go on and on.
Firstly, let me draw your attention to Revelations 146-7 and Daniel 244-45. Read these chapters and verses and you will
find that neither the Scripture nor the Kingdom on earth were not to be found on earth at that time. What was to
happen after this arrangement read Revelations 184 where were you to go, look at Isaiah 22 and Micah4 1 .
When the Saints came to Utah, there was a Mr Bridger, a mountain man who had lived here for years, trapping and
selling animal skins. There was actually a community of such people living here trapping and carrying the skins to
market, over a thousand miles away - to St. Louis. It is said that they told the Saints that they would pay them $1,000
for the first ear of corn that they could grow here as it froze here every single month of the year.
In the Valley (or Salt Lake Valley) some of the Saints wanted to go on to California, but Brigham Young said "This is the
place. I have seen it in a vision. This is an excellent place to be led to by a prophet."
One day walking around, he struck his staff on the ground and said "This is where the Temple for our God is to be built
some day."
There were only about a hundred and fifty of these poor people; how strange that anybody could think such a thing.
But the United States sent an army of 40,000 armed men, with splendid weapons, and all trained fighters. When the
Army was within 100 miles of Salt Lake City the word went out that everybody should collect to SLC to prepare to go to
meet the army. My father was one of those soldiers. When they were about to set off from camp, Brigham Young
came to address them and said "Brothers. If you will keep good order and attend to our prayers, you will whip them
without firing a gun. There will not be a man of you lost."
The government spent $40,000 on this. After peace was declared and they had settled here for some time the soldiers'
opinion was "Nine months of winter and three months of cold weather. Let those God-damn Mormons have it!" They
did not think that this land was fighting for.

What did Brigham Young have to say "Brothers. This country will become the finest country in the world. You will be
able to raise anything that you want." I draw your attention to Isaiah 37 once a desert but now blossoming like a rose.
Any traveller s through this country from East or West, North or South, they all praise this area for being so beautiful,
and healthy.
The world pre-judges Joseph Smith because he said that he had seen the Father and Son and had spoken to them, and
that angels had visited him and taught him and prepared him to be an instrument in God's hand to spread His word in
these Latter Days. That was the reason for the persecution. The practise of having multiple wives had not begun at
that time.
Read Joel 228 -29. From this we understand that the Spirit of God is poured generously onto God's people. If you believe
in the Bible and promise to do so, as we read in Peter ii 1 21 that God's holy people shall speak as they are inspired by
the Holy Spirit with prophesies that they had quoted would come in the future or in the Latter Days.
Ask yourself, isn't it time that the Angel brought the message to the people on this planet? The last part of
Nebuchadnezzar's dream that the Kingdom was to govern and that rock would rupture from the earth and fall to fill
the whole earth. The question is, has the time come for this to happen? As Daniel said, somebody must be a sacrifice
in God's hand and John had been baptised and prepared to come ahead of Jesus Christ, Saviour of the world.
What reason do we have not to accept Joseph Smith as an instrument in God's hand to come to prepare for the
Second Coming? The promise is that we will be given proof, so that we can know what is true or not. Read John 319. If
Joseph Smith is a prophet, sent by God, remember that you are refusing God and not Joseph Smith. The Bible says that
a cruel retribution will follow for the people of the earth for ignoring God's words. Joseph Smith and no other, held
God's hand in 1820. Joseph Smith had the first revelation and was taught by angels, several times up until 1830, when
they formed a group with six members and as they had been taught. They called it the Church of Jesus Christ Latter
Day saints. As Noah had called to warn the inhabitants of the earth in those times that destruction was to be brought
upon the wicked people of earth. But who believed him? You know the story. And who believed John talking about the
son of God? Just a small wise group. The deluge came to seal Noah's words. Jesus Christ was the son of God. It did not
matter who believed or dis-believed. It was true.
The world has received the evidence of Joseph Smith and his followers, for 95 years, know that the scripture had been
restored and Joseph Smith's prophesy verified. But who believes them? Only a small handful, to preach to all the
people of the world. But it is true that there are thousands in Utah who testify that they know that Joseph Smith was
one of the prophets and that God had honoured him with His presence in these days just as in Abraham's days.
My father was very keen to come from the Old Country before the sea closed so that it would be dangerous to cross
the sea. He sought to escape before war, hunger and plagues struck the people of the world. I thought that these
things would have happened before now, but God has His own time to do His will.
About 25 years ago I worked in SLC and stayed at the same hotel as a Catholic. We started talking in a friendly manner
about religion. The government was unhappy with the Saints at that time so I did not volunteer to speak about
religion. He asked "What's happening in your religion? Was it handed down from the Apostle Paul?" "Well, didn't your
religion exist before Jesus born?" Yes! Who persecuted and stoned the Saints? Not the different religions which
existed at that time. In what way did they get their authority from Peter? The big question!
Constantine the Great, his mother was a Christian, the daughter of Coelgodebog(?) and his father was a pagan from
Rome. When Constantine came to power he felt and wanted to join up all the religions so in the year 314AD he
decreed that all the world's religions were to come to the city called Nice, France. With a view to assuring peace they
would create one religion, which everyone could agree to, thus ensuring peace. This would be called Catholicism or
General Unity. In Welsh Peter had died 200 years before this mix-up was to happen. One of our priests met with one
of the Catholic priests to talk. The Catholic said that the big effort was to be between us and you, and the other
religions do not count as they are just derived from us and it is likely that the children will turn their backs on them.
My father joined the Saints on May 24th 1846. I arrived in Utah in 1856, almost 59 years ago. I have seen many changes
and much persecution and mocking of the Saints. This is cruel and unfounded and it has poisoned the minds of
thousands of people across the world so that they cannot read or listen to anything that comes from the Saints. Many
say good things, and like Nebuchadnezzar, they worship the god of Daniel. But they would not come together to
worship the god of Daniel. He had a god whom he had worshipped all of his life.

Now I can testify to you in all seriousness and truth that I know without a shadow of doubt that I am certain that
Joseph Smith was God's chosen prophet and the vision of Joseph Smith is what I have passed on to you.
Most of it has already come true, the remaining part is sure to be realised.
I will not judge you at all if you do not believe what I have written. If one is to judge God's deeds then He has to open
our eyes so that we can see and understand His words. We will get evidence as Jesus told Peter "The blood made this
known to you but it was my father that was the one"(???). Read. Understand. Be wise. Do not refuse the incitement of
the Holy Spirit. Judge for yourself.
Be great!
I remain in the kindest way
Your cousin
R.D. Roberts

letters.title: Humphrey Jones (Bryfdir) to Robert D. Roberts - 27 July 1917
letters.language: English supplied translation/transcription; underlying letter language not established
letters.suppliedText:
500061-500063
Preswylfa
Rhiwbryfdir
Blaenau Ffestiniog
N. Wales
July 27th 1917
My Dear Uncle
Thanks to the local postmaster, I received your letter yesterday. I find a letter from a distant land to very interesting –
especially as it comes from a branch of the Llety and Erw Fawr family. I have spoken often about you and made
inquiries.
I did not receive the letter which you said that you had sent me a few years ago – I have only received a Christmas
greeting from your sister (my aunt) and then she did not include a return address so that I could acknowledge receipt.
I remember your brother well; he stayed for quite a while with my mother (who is still alive and 83 years old).
David D. Roberts (son of David Roberts of Dorfil Street) is no longer in this area; he moved to work in Liverpool due to
the recession in the slate mines. I will probably see him soon and will be sure to say that you were inquiring about him
and asking about the old family.
With this letter I attach an issue of {the journal} Cymru. In it you will see a photograph of me and be able to read a bit
about my career. (I have another copy if any other member of your family wants a copy – just let me know in your next
letter – a letter which I hope to receive very shortly).
My mother is not at hand and so I cannot immediately find out the family information which you wanted and so I
cannot include this with my letter. I will however have formed a full genealogy for you in just a few days.
We are trying to live our lives with the backdrop of War. We spent all our money on our two eldest sons – one is
working in a bank, the other works in a store, but we have to yield them to the army. I have no idea what will become
of them – their mother and I daily "fear for the worst and hope for the best".
By the way, my wife was over in the States for seven years. She graduated with honours from Albany College. We have
a very comfortable home, were it not for the shadow of War. We are well-known across the country and have
featured often - on paper and on stage. Anything that you have sent should certainly have got to me – I get letters
from all over the world with just the simple address "Bryfdir, Blaenau Ffestiniog". You must bear in mind though that
the Germans have sunk many British and American ships recently and a letter is easily lost as it makes its way over the
waves.
I would like you to send me the addresses of more of the Old Family in Utah and I trust, dear Uncle, that you will
continue to write to me, despite the weight of old age pressing on your shoulders.
I do not know what will become of us in the slate district. If the war lasts another winter, I believe that every slate
mine will have closed (at least temporarily). That would be a huge loss but the wheels have been turning slowly for
many a year.
I must not tire you with an over-long first letter. I cannot stress enough how happy I was to hear from you. I will now
be like the fabled watchman on the tower looking expectedly towards the rising of the sun from the land of the
darkness.
Wishing you a good and restful afternoon.
Your nephew
Humphrey Jones (Bryfdir)
Mr R.D. Roberts, Logan City, Utah

letter-080 humphrey jones (bryfdir) to robert d. roberts - 27 july 1917 humphrey jones (bryfdir) robert d. roberts 27 july 1917   pdf page 109 500061-500063
preswylfa
rhiwbryfdir
blaenau ffestiniog
n. wales
july 27th 1917
my dear uncle
thanks to the local postmaster, i received your letter yesterday. i find a letter from a distant land to very interesting –
especially as it comes from a branch of the llety and erw fawr family. i have spoken often about you and made
inquiries.
i did not receive the letter which you said that you had sent me a few years ago – i have only received a christmas
greeting from your sister (my aunt) and then she did not include a return address so that i could acknowledge receipt.
i remember your brother well; he stayed for quite a while with my mother (who is still alive and 83 years old).
david d. roberts (son of david roberts of dorfil street) is no longer in this area; he moved to work in liverpool due to
the recession in the slate mines. i will probably see him soon and will be sure to say that you were inquiring about him
and asking about the old family.
with this letter i attach an issue of {the journal} cymru. in it you will see a photograph of me and be able to read a bit
about my career. (i have another copy if any other member of your family wants a copy – just let me know in your next
letter – a letter which i hope to receive very shortly).
my mother is not at hand and so i cannot immediately find out the family information which you wanted and so i
cannot include this with my letter. i will however have formed a full genealogy for you in just a few days.
we are trying to live our lives with the backdrop of war. we spent all our money on our two eldest sons – one is
working in a bank, the other works in a store, but we have to yield them to the army. i have no idea what will become
of them – their mother and i daily "fear for the worst and hope for the best".
by the way, my wife was over in the states for seven years. she graduated with honours from albany college. we have
a very comfortable home, were it not for the shadow of war. we are well-known across the country and have
featured often - on paper and on stage. anything that you have sent should certainly have got to me – i get letters
from all over the world with just the simple address "bryfdir, blaenau ffestiniog". you must bear in mind though that
the germans have sunk many british and american ships recently and a letter is easily lost as it makes its way over the
waves.
i would like you to send me the addresses of more of the old family in utah and i trust, dear uncle, that you will
continue to write to me, despite the weight of old age pressing on your shoulders.
i do not know what will become of us in the slate district. if the war lasts another winter, i believe that every slate
mine will have closed (at least temporarily). that would be a huge loss but the wheels have been turning slowly for
many a year.
i must not tire you with an over-long first letter. i cannot stress enough how happy i was to hear from you. i will now
be like the fabled watchman on the tower looking expectedly towards the rising of the sun from the land of the
darkness.
wishing you a good and restful afternoon.
your nephew
humphrey jones (bryfdir)
mr r.d. roberts, logan city, utah
